deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (my interpretation, which the page's notation strongly supports). The page is dated 'Göttingen, October 1862'. Riemann is working with an unramified two-sheeted covering T~ of a genus-p surface T, which is the setting of Prym's theory; Prym was Riemann's student, and his work began from Riemann's suggestions around 1862-63.

The covering has genus 2p-1. It is given a canonical dissection by the cuts a_nu, b_nu and a'_nu, b'_nu for nu = 1..p-1 (the two lifts of T's cycles), plus a_p, b_p.

Two families of normalized integrals appear, in Riemann's 1857 conventions (periods pi*i on the a-cycles):
- u_1..u_p are the integrals of T pulled back to T~, with period matrix a_{nu,mu}.
- v_1..v_{p-1} are the anti-invariant (Prym) integrals, with v' = -v on the other sheet and period matrix b_{nu,mu}.

The theta functions are:
- theta(u), the theta of T;
- theta(v), in p-1 variables, the Prym theta;
- Omega(u_1..u_p; v_1..v_{p-1}), the theta function of the genus-(2p-1) surface T~ written in these adapted coordinates.

The first two lines fix orientation conventions for the cuts: b crosses a from the positive to the negative side, and vice versa.

PART A: zeros of the Prym theta. This is the analogue of Riemann's 1857 paragraph 22 argument.
- Consider theta(v - e) as a function on the dissected surface T~'. Its zeros are 2p-2 points (=2(p-1)); call the values of the integrals there beta_nu^mu and alpha_nu^mu.
- Integrating v_nu d log theta around the boundary gives int (v_nu^+ - v_nu^-) d log theta = 2 pi i Sum_{mu=1}^{2p-2} beta_nu^mu.
- Across a_nu and a'_nu the jump of v_nu is +-pi i. The quasi-periodicity of theta gives int d log theta = -2(v_nu - e_nu) - 2 pi i h_nu (resp. h'_nu), where h, h' are integers from the branch of the logarithm. Here v_nu is evaluated at the start of b_nu.
- Across b_nu and b'_nu the integrand produces -+2 int v_nu dv_nu, which evaluates to v^2 - (v + pi i)^2. It also produces terms b_{nu,nu} g_nu 2 pi i, where g, g' are again integers.
- Across b_mu and b'_mu (mu != nu) the contributions combine to -b_{nu,mu}(g_mu + g'_mu) 2 pi i.
- Adding everything and dividing by the doubled count gives e_nu = 1/2 Sum_{mu=1}^{2p-2} beta_nu^mu + (h_nu + h'_nu)/2 pi i + Sum_{mu=1}^p (g_mu + g'_mu)/2 b_{nu,mu}.
- In words: the zero divisor D determines e as one half of its Abel-Prym image, up to periods. This is the Prym analogue of 'sum of zeros = e + Riemann constant'.

PART B: the same divisor read through T's integrals.
- The same boundary computation with u_nu gives Sum alpha_nu^mu = (h'_nu - h_nu) pi i + Sum_mu a_{nu,mu}(g'_mu - g_mu) - 2 a_{nu,p} g_p.
- For nu = p it gives Sum alpha_p^mu = -h_p pi i + Sum a_{p,mu}(g'_mu - g_mu) - 2 a_{p,p} g_p, up to a constant.
- The constant is fixed by a normalization: e = 0 and h + h' = g + g' = 0. This gives Sum alpha_nu = a_{p,nu} and Sum alpha_p = pi i + a_{p,p}, with several crossed-out attempts on the page.
- Then theta(r_1..r_{p-1}) = 0 when r_nu = 1/2 Sum beta_nu^mu + ....
- The parity of h_p (0 or 1 mod 2) is tied to theta being even or odd ('gerade/ungerade'). The page states 1/2(Sum alpha_1, ..., Sum alpha_p) ≡ 1/2(eps_1 pi i + Sum eps'_mu a_{1,mu}, ...) with eps'_p = 1 and eps_p + h_p ≡ 1 mod 2.

CONCLUSION (vanishing theorem). theta(r_1..r_{p-1}) = 0 iff r ≡ 1/2 Sum (Abel-Prym images of 2p-2 points), where the 2p-2 points satisfy the following: their image under T's Abel map is congruent to the half-period (1/2 a_{1,p}, ..., 1/2 a_{p,p} + eps pi i/2), with eps = 0 or 1.

In modern terms, the Prym theta divisor is the locus of half Abel-Prym images of degree-(2p-2) divisors whose norm lies in a fixed class, the canonical class twisted by the half-period of the covering. There are two parity components, labelled by eps. This is the content of Mumford's description Xi = {L in Nm^{-1}(K), h^0(L) even}.

PART C: four 'unabhängig' (proportionality) statements.
1) Omega(2u_1..2u_p; 0) / [theta(u) theta(u_1, ..., u_{p-1}, u_p + pi i/2)] is independent of u. Modern form: the pullback of the covering's theta to pi*J is theta(u) theta(u + eta), with eta the 2-torsion point of the covering.
2) Omega(0; 2v) / theta(v)^2 is independent of v. Modern form: the covering's theta restricted to the Prym variety is (const) times the square of the Prym theta, i.e. Theta~|_P = 2 Xi.
3) Omega(u - u' - a_{p,nu}; v - v' - 2e) / [theta(v - e) theta(v' + e)] is independent of e. This is a two-point (addition-type) factorization.
4) Omega(u - u' - 2c; v - v') / [theta(u - u' - c) theta(c_1, ..., c_p + pi i/2)] is independent of c, provided theta(c) = 0.
3*) A reparametrized version of 3) via v - v' - 2s = 2e: Omega(u - u'; 2s) / [theta((v - v')/2 + s) theta((v' - v)/2 - s)] is independent of s.

An auxiliary vanishing statement is also given: Omega(Sum alpha_nu^mu - (p-1) a_{p,nu}, Sum beta_nu^mu) = 0.

What these serve: they relate the theta function of the double cover to the theta of T and to the Prym theta. These are exactly the ingredients of what are now called the Schottky-Jung proportionalities.
errors: The line for Sum alpha_p^mu ends '-2a_{p,p} g_p 2 pi i'. The extra factor 2 pi i is inconsistent with the parallel formula for Sum alpha_nu (which has -2a_{nu,p} g_p) and with the b_p line; it looks like a slip.

The normalisation lines (e = 0, h + h' = g + g' = 0) are visibly tentative. Three successive versions of Sum alpha_nu and Sum alpha_p are given (one with +a_{p,nu}, one with -2a_{nu,p} g_p, one with +h_p pi i rather than -h_p pi i), with deletions; the sign of h_p is not consistent across them.
In the b_nu line the elementary evaluation v^2 - (v + pi i)^2 = -2 pi i v + pi^2 is left unsimplified. The pi^2 and b_{nu,nu} pi i constants are absorbed without comment into 'const'.

The proportionality claims 1)-4) are stated without proof. Claim 4) has a side condition theta(c) = 0 whose role is not explained. The intended characteristic of Omega is not specified, so the half-period shifts (pi i/2) can only be checked up to choice of characteristic.
The step from the period relations to 'theta(r) = 0 iff ...' asserts the converse (every such divisor gives a zero) without argument. Modern treatments need h^0 parity considerations for this.

results.what: Boundary-integral (d log theta) computation locating the 2p-2 zeros of the Prym theta on the double cover: e ≡ 1/2 (Abel-Prym image of the zero divisor) + half-periods
results.modern_name: Riemann vanishing theorem for Prym varieties / Abel-Prym map
results.usually_credited_to: Wirtinger (1895, Untersuchungen über Thetafunctionen); modern form Mumford (1974, Prym varieties I)

results.what: The Prym theta divisor described as half-images of degree-(2p-2) divisors whose image under T's Abel map is a fixed half-period, with two parity cases eps = 0, 1
results.modern_name: Mumford's description Xi = {L in Nm^{-1}(K_C): h^0 even}, with the two components of Nm^{-1}(K)

results.what: Omega(2u, 0) proportional to theta(u) theta(u + eta)
results.modern_name: Pullback of the theta divisor of the double cover to pi*J equals Theta + Theta_eta (Schottky-Jung type identity)
Restriction of the cover's theta to the Prym is 2 Xi (Schottky-Jung proportionality)

results.what: Factorizations 3), 3*), 4) of Omega at two-point arguments into products of Prym or base thetas
results.modern_name: Fay-type theta identities for unramified double covers

deep.surprise_reason: It is known that Riemann inspired Prym's theory and worked on two-sheeted covers around 1862. But explicit Schottky-Jung-type proportionalities (Omega(0,2v) ~ theta_P(v)^2, Omega(2u,0) ~ theta(u) theta(u+eta)) and a Prym version of the vanishing theorem with parity cases, in Riemann's hand in 1862, predate Schottky (1888), Wirtinger (1895) and Schottky-Jung (1909). That would be a notable precedence, though only sketched and unproved. I am not certain this Nachlass material has not already been discussed, so I am conservative.

checkable.asserts: Evaluation of the b_nu boundary term -2 int v dv across a jump of pi*i
The number of zeros of the Prym theta on the cover is 2p-2 = 2 dim(Prym)
Genus of the unramified double cover (2p-1) = genus of T (p) + Prym dimension (p-1), matching Omega's variables (u_1..u_p; v_1..v_{p-1})
p=1 analogue of claim 1): the theta of the double cover at 2u is proportional to theta(u) theta(u + half-period)
Trivial consistency of the reparametrization v - v' - 2s = 2e used to pass from 3) to 3*): e = (v - v')/2 - s

transcription_corrections: The normalization line probably reads 'e_nu = 0, e_p = 0 | h_nu + h'_nu = g_nu + g'_nu = 0' rather than 'e_1 = a_1, ..., e_p = 0'.
The Sum alpha_p line indeed shows '-2a_{p,p} g_p 2 pi i + const'; it is retained, but appears to be a slip.
The garbled start of the parity line is likely 'wenn theta gerade ... h_p ≡ 0 mod 2 / ungerade h_p ≡ 1 mod 2'.
'Gruppe 0 (0)^{p-1}' is likely a characteristic notation (0 over (0)^{p-1}).
In 3*) the denominator is theta((v_nu - v'_nu)/2 + s_nu) theta((v'_nu - v_nu)/2 - s_nu); the numerator's second slot is 2 s_nu.
